posts.name: TheCraftyCurler
posts.cooked:
Okay, I'll put my nerdgasm here! 

The "Star Trek" fan in me has always had an affinity for the non-human characters, and that affinity began right away in the base game. Tempest has always had a special place in my heart, and Omnitron-X was very quickly soon to follow. They are, easily, my favorite characters/hero decks to play. Like, my fondness for how they're written is trong enough to the point that if a live-action series of this comic ever came to fruitition, I would do everything in my power to audition for the character. So you can only imagine how that snippet of him being a Katy Perry fan made my gay heart just sing (no pun intended). I'm eagerly looking forward to seeing what, if any, his promo for an alternate version of him as a Prime Warden might be (same for Omnitron-U).

On an unrelated note, I'm totally okay with every single comic featuring Tyler in only a tank top shirt. Dem guns, yo! lol, Just sayin'! (And I totally ship him with Wraith, too.) 

As for Absolute Zero... not knowing all too much about the character, I REALLY liked his monologue and the scene between him and Tachyon. For someone confined to certain spaces for the rest of his life, it's great (and in a weird way, sad) to see that how I pictured him being mostly introspective and alone with his thoughts is more accurate than not. Also, mad props for Tachyon's speech about how far they've all come. GtG is doing an amazing job getting to the heart of their characters with the writing, and I'm loving every character-building minute of it.

However, indepedent of all this, I must say that the few times my friends and I played the game against Progeny, he didn't seem to be THAT big of a challenge. At least, not enough to warrant this epic of a villain storyline. Is that just me? Honestly.

Oblivaeon has the Aeon men, who look like robots, and he found his scions and offered them "collars". Then there is the idea of him destroying and then potentially reforming everything. What if this is all about control? What if the idea of "divine dominance" is at play here, the idea of a god like being who needs absolute control and authority over all things.

 

The heroes and the villains of the muliverse are getting too powerful though, threatening not the being directly, but it's idea of its own control. They can defy it and that is unacceptable and they must die. That makes Ra's blow even more insulting. They not only defy it, but actually injured it!

 

And we have villains that play into that trope.

 

Voss used his sciece to genetically engineer soldiers he controlled. Dawn brings people back from the dead to continue to serve her, they can't die without her permission. Chokepoint controls and manipulates the world around her. The Matriarch controls birds andif the Tactics info is remebered correctly the minds of others, and the Mask according to one of the new stories, is trying to control the Matriarch. Kismet controls fate and luck, to an extent. Kaagra has the Bloodsworn Gladiators who serve her, bound to the Colusseum.
